Preserve the SAME recognizable person, face, age, skin, hair, expression, LEFTWARD three-quarter gaze and identical garment. Outpaint both complete shoulders and upper arms. Images 2,3,4 are materials only: aged warm metal, cold gothic material, cloth/bone; do not copy their characters or accessories.
CRITICAL matched series framing: square canvas, head small enough: hair crown at 10% height, eyes at 30%, anatomical chin at 50%, head width 36–38%. Head horizontal center 50%. Both shoulders completely visible with generous transparent side margins, silhouette inside x8–92%. Same camera distance for every portrait. Bust to upper chest, lower torso cropped only by bottom. Do not crop sides, zoom into face, or auto-trim transparency. No waist, hands, new props. Preserve natural proportions. Head size consistency more important than filling canvas.
Fine dry-brush gothic painting, sculptural volume, matte skin, grouped hair, coarse worn cloth, subtle irregular strokes following form; deep chiaroscuro, light upper front-left. Muted earth charcoal bone colors. Not photograph, glossy 3D or cartoon.
Actual transparent PNG alpha outside silhouette, no black or white background, painted checkerboard, frame, labels, halo. Keep dark clothing and internal shadows opaque. One square portrait.
Image 5 is a previous edit that is TOO CLOSE. Zoom the entire bust OUT by 20 percent compared to image 5. Move crown down to 10%, anatomical chin to50%. Leave wide empty transparent side columns. Preserve identity from image1. Need smaller head, complete shoulders, no silhouette touching sides.
